name: Uganda unified poultry health schedule, DRAFT v0.1
status: DRAFT. Must be reviewed and signed off by a licensed Ugandan veterinarian or poultry health specialist before release to farmers.

conventions.age_days: Day 1 is hatch day. 'Week N' in source charts is mapped to day 7*N (end of week N).

priority_levels.core: Present in most sources; do not skip.
priority_levels.recommended: In at least one Ugandan source; default ON.
priority_levels.optional: Depends on region, vet choice, or farm history; default OFF, farmer or vet toggles.

due_window.note: Configurable per step. Reminder fires the day before and on the due day.

conventions.hatchery_steps: Steps with location=hatchery are shown as 'confirm done at hatchery', not as reminders.
conventions.catch_up_rule: On batch registration at age A: steps with age_days < A become 'assumed done at source, please confirm'. Steps due but not confirmed show as overdue. Do not back-fill silently.

sources.UPBL: Ugachick Poultry Breeders, broiler and layer vaccination programs (ugachickpoultrybreeders.com)
sources.MAAIF: MAAIF Poultry Training Manual for Extension Workers in Uganda, Aug 2019 (Table 29 layers, Table 30 broilers, sections 4.6.1 and 4.7.3)
sources.AARON: Aaron Vet Farms Ltd, vaccine guide for Uganda

handling_rules: Keep vaccine water below 20 C and vaccinate in the morning.
Thirst birds for 1-2 hours before drinking-water vaccination; all vaccine water should be consumed within 1-2 hours.
Use non-chlorinated water for drinking-water vaccines and do not disinfect drinkers after washing them on vaccination day (MAAIF).
Avoid antibiotics on vaccination days. Only multivitamins are recommended.
Vaccination does not guarantee protection. It must be combined with nutrition, biosecurity, and stockmanship.
Schedule changes only after consulting a vet who knows the local disease situation.

steps.label: Day-old hatchery vaccination (ND, IB, IBD)
vaccine_options: ND Clone 30 + Ma5, or ND C2 + IB 4/91 (coarse spray)
steps.notes: Given at hatchery. App should ask the farmer to confirm it was done and record what the hatchery used.

steps.label: ND + IB (first farm dose)
steps.notes: UPBL's broiler chart relies on the day-1 hatchery combination and has no day-7 dose. If the hatchery already gave ND+IB, the vet may adjust. Vet decision.

steps.label: Gumboro (IBD) booster
steps.notes: MAAIF broiler card lists a second Gumboro dose at day 21. Whether it is still needed after a vector IBD vaccine at the hatchery is a vet decision.

steps.label: ND + IB booster
steps.notes: MAAIF lists it as routine. UPBL lists it as optional, for birds kept beyond 42 days. Treat as high priority if the batch will be kept past about 35 days.

steps.label: Day-old hatchery vaccination (Marek's, ND, IBD, IB)
steps.notes: Given at hatchery. Marek's must be given at day 1. App should ask the farmer to confirm.

steps.label: ND + IB (first farm dose)
steps.notes: Not in UPBL's chart, which relies on the day-1 combination. Vet decision.

steps.label: Gumboro (IBD) booster
steps.notes: Only MAAIF lists a week-3 Gumboro dose. UPBL gives one farm dose at week 2. Vet decision.

steps.label: Fowl pox
steps.notes: Check for a 'take' (small scab at the site) about a week later.

steps.label: Fowl typhoid dose 1
vaccine_options: Inactivated Salmonella vaccine (SE + ST + SG strains)
steps.notes: Aaron lists SC. UPBL and MAAIF list IM. Follow the product label.

steps.label: Fowl typhoid dose 2
vaccine_options: Inactivated Salmonella vaccine (SE + ST + SG strains)

steps.label: Inactivated ND + IB pre-lay booster (optional)
steps.notes: MAAIF says killed vaccine may be used at weeks 16-18 and ND+IB repeated after about 6 months. Only if the vet chooses the killed-vaccine route instead of the 6-weekly live booster.

steps.label: Fowl cholera dose 1 (outbreak areas only)
steps.notes: Only for farms or areas with previous outbreaks. Offer as a toggle. MAAIF lists week 11 and week 18.

steps.label: Deworm
steps.notes: UPBL: weeks 9 and 15. MAAIF: weeks 8 and 16. Follow the product label.

steps.label: First beak trim (precision)
steps.notes: Often done at the hatchery. Do not schedule close to a vaccination day. Give vitamin K in water around trimming, per MAAIF.

steps.label: Second beak trim
steps.notes: MAAIF says 8-10 weeks. UPBL says week 10. Birds should be healthy and not recently vaccinated.

recurring.label: ND + IB live booster (lay phase)
recurring.notes: UPBL: repeat IB every 4-6 weeks, alternating Ma5 and 4/91. MAAIF: live ND+IB about every 6 weeks. Aaron: ND booster about every 6 weeks. Default 6 weeks, editable by the vet. Ends at off-lay (weeks 72-80).

recurring.label: Deworm (lay phase)
recurring.notes: UPBL: repeat every 6-8 weeks. Default 8 weeks. Do not schedule on the same day as a vaccination.

dual_purpose_and_local.note: Not yet modelled as programs. MAAIF guidance for later phases.
improved_breeds: Egg strain: use the layer program.
Meat strain: use the broiler-style program; MAAIF says vaccination stops at 4 weeks.
local_chicken: ND in week 1, at 6 weeks, at 3 months, then adults twice a year.
Fowl pox, Marek's and IB also advised.
Deworm monthly after 2 months of age.
Thermostable ND strains (I-2, V4) are used for village flocks in hot conditions.

open_questions_for_vet: Broiler day 7 ND+IB and day 21 Gumboro: needed when the hatchery gives the day-1 combination including a vector IBD vaccine?
Broiler day 28 ND+IB: routine (MAAIF) or only if kept beyond 42 days (UPBL)?
Layer pre-lay: 6-weekly live ND+IB or inactivated ND+IB(+EDS) at weeks 16-18?
Fowl pox second dose (MAAIF shows week 10 as well as week 6): include?
Avian encephalomyelitis (AE) and EDS: not in the Ugandan sources reviewed, but common in international layer programs. Include as optional?
Coccidiosis prevention (a program vs. vaccine vs. anticoccidials) is not covered here.
